key_insight: A spatially grounded concept bottleneck model uses weak lesion delineations to make breast ultrasound predictions more anatomically plausible and trustworthy.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve how AI supports breast ultrasound diagnosis by linking predictions to clinically meaningful regions and concepts, not just final labels.
method: Derives two zones from each lesion mask: an in-lesion region for morphology concepts and a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena.
Trains concept maps with a grouped spatial grounding objective.
Uses a linear bottleneck classifier to keep concept-based predictions semantically faithful.
evidence_signal: Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the model improved diagnostic AUROC, concept macro-AUROC, and spatial alignment of concept evidence; a Train-corrupt/Test-clean stress test assessed the effect of annotation quality.
watch_item: Performance and explainability depend on the quality of lesion supervision, so coarse or corrupted annotations may still limit real-world reliability.
paper_title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
